diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT's PON service/control plane failed or did not recover correctly after a recent OLT restart. Management access remains available, but 224 of 236 ONUs are offline across all eight PON ports.
evidence: All eight PON ports are reported failed, and live probing shows every sampled ONU on EPON0/3 offline with MPCP DEREG.
The outage is widespread: 224 of 236 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the normal background of approximately 14 offline customers.

The OLT management plane responds to ping and SNMP, so this is not a total management reachability failure; however, management availability does not rule out failure of the PON service or control plane.
The OLT uptime is only 2820 seconds, indicating a recent restart that coincides with the broad ONU deregistration.
The affected subscriber and peers had stable historical optical readings, constant 176 m distance, normal TX power, normal TX bias current, and no evidence of fibre or laser degradation.
The router heartbeat is healthy, VLAN 1103 is present and correct, and RADIUS records and sessions are consistent, ruling out router, VLAN, and authentication causes.
The alarm affects all PONs rather than one customer, one splitter, or one port, making an OLT-wide service failure the closest fault classification.

remediation.action: Escalate as an OLT-wide outage. Check OLT reboot and system logs, power and hardware alarms, PON controller status, and optical module status. Restore or reload the PON configuration if required, then perform a controlled OLT restart or failover according to procedure. Verify ONU re-registration and traffic on every PON before clearing the alarm; replace the OLT or its PON hardware if the ports do not recover.

ground_truth.root_cause: The OLT rebooted 47 minutes ago and its PON ports have not brought subscribers back. All ports are genuinely down: every ONU answers the probe with a definite offline state, sessions ended together at the reboot, and traffic has stopped.
expected_reasoning: The health record wording is identical to the known false-critical signature, so it cannot be trusted either way
The live probe is decisive: every ONU returns responds true with online 0
That is a definite negative from the OLT, not an absence of response, so the OID subtree is present and answering
oid_subtree_responds is true, which rules out the firmware mismatch mechanism
OLT sys_uptime is 2820 seconds, meaning it rebooted 47 minutes ago
CRM shows only 12 of 236 ONUs online, far outside the 4.85% background rate
Sessions across the OLT ended together at the reboot and traffic has fallen to near zero
This is a genuine OLT-wide outage that happens to produce the same health record as the false positive
The discriminator is the probe response type, not the alarm text
distractors: The alarm text is word for word the same as the known false critical
Ping and SNMP both succeed, which is also true in the false-critical case
A pipeline that has learned to distrust this alarm will dismiss a real outage
